key_insight: A five-qubit hybrid quantum neural network achieved 55.4–59.8% suspicious-class F1 on IBM hardware, but classical XGBoost remained best at 61.4%.
engineering_relevance: Classical angle generation paired with a small quantum circuit offers a hardware-tested approach to trade surveillance, without demonstrating quantum advantage.
method: Compare QKNN, QSVM, a 20-qubit QNN and a five-qubit hybrid QNN against classical classifiers.
Use shared stratified train/test data and 20-feature ANOVA and PCA representations.
Test QKNN and QSVM under simulated noise and deploy the hybrid QNN on ibm_fez.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 1,000 synthetic accounts with 20% suspicious cases and an 800/200 train/test split; the hybrid model outperformed six of eight classical configurations.
watch_item: Results on a small synthetic dataset do not establish real-world AML performance or quantum advantage.
paper_title: Hybrid Quantum Algorithms for Trade Surveillance Analytics
